title: Cost Composer: initiative roadmap for batching, caching, and quantization
creator: Maya Chen
description: Consolidate and execute a coordinated initiative to reduce per-token inference costs through three levers: smarter batching, tiered KV prefix caching, and safe quantization profiles. The goal is a repeatable program that ships measurable unit-economics wins (target: 18-25% overall cost reduction on cold workloads) while preserving P99 latency SLOs and minimizing quality regressions for top 20 customer prompts.
goals_okrs: OKR 1: Reduce average per-token cost for 95th percentile workloads by 20% by end of Q2
OKR 2: Keep P99 latency regression <= 5% after deploying batching and cache improvements
OKR 3: Establish continuous experiment harness and rollout guardrails for quantization with automated quality checks
milestones: M1: Experiment grid defined and instrumented (2025-01-31)
M2: Initial batching heuristics & CVM in runtime deployed to canary (2025-02-14)
M3: Tiered KV cache TTLs and eviction policy landed (2025-02-28)
M4: Quantization profiles validated on internal eval set and guardrails implemented (2025-03-21)
M5: Canary -> gradual rollout plan executed with rollback SLOs (2025-04-10)
experiment_grid_summary: Axis A (Batching): continuous-batching vs sized-batching vs request-level batching disabled
Axis B (Cache): no-cache vs single-tier TTL(30s) vs tiered TTLs(5s/60s) with prefix hotness sampling
Axis C (Quant): FP16 baseline vs 4-bit QAT safe vs 4-bit post-training with per-layer clipping
Metrics: cost/token, P50/P95/P99 latency, top-10 prompt BLEU-like similarity delta, customer error rate
acceptance_criteria: Experiment results stored in centralized dashboard with historical baselines
Validated rollout policy: automated rollback on latency or quality regression thresholds
At least two production routes (hosted + dedicated) demonstrate >=15% cost reduction without >5% P99 latency increase
Quantization profiles include per-model fallback mapping and documented quality deltas for top customer prompts
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Aggressive batching increases tail latency -> Mitigation: latency-aware dynamic batching cap and per-route SLOs
Risk: Quantization causes subtle output drift -> Mitigation: automated prompt-set evals + canary traffic gating + quick-fallback to float variant
Risk: Cache TTL tuning harms freshness-sensitive apps -> Mitigation: route-level cache opt-out and metric tagging for cache-hit vs stale responses
updates: 2025-01-16: Kickoff with SRE, Runtime, and Eval teams. Agreed on initial success metrics and ownership.
2025-01-28: Instrumentation schema landed (ENG-4182). Added cost/token and per-route cache-hit tags to telemetry.
2025-02-10: Batching prototype shipped to canary. Early signal: 12% cost drop for short sequences but P99 increased by 6% on one route. Decided to implement latency caps before broader rollout.
2025-02-18: Tiered KV cache design approved in architecture review. Action: add sampling-based hot-prefix detection (ENG-5370).
2025-02-20: Quantization validation suite finished running for two top-customer models. One model shows 3% semantic drift on long-form prompts; flagged for QAT.
Next steps: finalize dynamic batching cap, finish TTL tuning experiment, and prepare canary rollout checklist for runtime-1.20
notes: Decision log: prefer incremental conservative changes over large cross-cutting optimizations to minimize customer impact.
Trade-off: higher caching TTLs yield cost wins but increase risk of stale completions; plan includes route-level opt-out and signal tagging.
SLA considerations: Dedicated customers with strict latency SLOs will be excluded from aggressive batching profiles by default.
